findings.what: Example 9.5's whole synthesis scheme is absent. The book draws six structures across two rows -- 4-nitrotoluene -Br2-> 2-bromo-4-nitrotoluene -Sn/HCl-> the amine -NaNO2/HCl, 273-278 K-> the N2Cl salt, then down via H2O/H3PO2 to 2-bromotoluene and -KMnO4/OH-> 2-bromobenzoic acid (COOH). The render shows only the question line 'How will you convert 4-nitrotoluene to 2-bromobenzoic acid ?' and the labels 'Example 9.5 / Solution' in an otherwise empty box.

The Summary's second paragraph is cut off after 'Amines are usually formed from nitro compounds, halides, amides, imides, etc.'. The book continues: 'They exhibit hydrogen bonding which influence their physical properties. In alkylamines, a combination of electron releasing, steric and H-bonding factors influence the stability of the substituted ammonium cations in protic polar solvents and thus affect the basic nature of amines. Alkyl amines are found to be stronger bases than ammonia. In aromatic amines, electron releasing and withdrawing groups, respectively increase and decrease their basic character. Aniline is a weaker base'. None of that is in the render.

The prime marks in the Summary's amine formulae are lost and replaced by runs of cent signs: the book's 'R2NH or R-NHR' and tertiary amines by R3N, RNR'R" or R2NR'' renders as 'R2NH or R-NHR¢and tertiaryamines by R3N,RNR¢R¢¢¢¢¢¢¢ ¢¢¢or R2NR¢.¢.¢.¢.¢.' -- the R' / R'' formulae cannot be read.

Word spaces are dropped at several line joins in the Summary: 'replacement ofhydrogen', 'hydrogen atom ofammonia', 'primary amine.Secondary amines', 'tertiaryamines', 'known assimple amines', 'mixed amines if thegroups', 'one unsharedelectron pair'.

findings.what: The Intext Question 9.9 panel has lost its box and heading style: the book sets it in a framed panel with a red tab and the script heading 'Intext Question' at top right, with '9.9 Convert' and the two items indented. The render prints 'Intext Question', '9.9', 'Convert' as three plain unframed lines of body text between the Example box and the Summary. The (i) and (ii) labels and both question texts are intact.

findings.what: The Summary's bold run-in terms (Amines, R-NH2, primary amine, Secondary amines, tertiary amines, R2NH, R3N, Lewis bases) are set in light grey roman instead of bold black, so they no longer read as the defined terms.

The bottom 55 per cent of the page is empty below the Summary box. Part of it is explained by the two missing blocks above, but I cannot tell whether anything else from book page 277 was meant to sit there.

note: Compared block by block against book page 277. Present and correct: the two-line carry-over paragraph at the top, the Example 9.5 question line, both Intext Question 9.9 items with their (i)/(ii) labels, the Summary heading and its first paragraph (apart from the garbling noted), and the folio '277 Amines' at the bottom right. The Example box keeps its blue tab but is now only two lines tall. I could not judge whether the Summary text stops because of a truncation or because the following page carries the rest -- the next page should be checked for the continuation.
